cars.generation: Original Edward Turner V8 fibreglass sports roadster family
cars.variant: SP250 — May 1960 base production application, manual
cars.specification_market: Original Daimler/RAC production application, FIA 20 GT, 14-page file. Cover/engine/transmission/chassis/options and production certificate PDF1/3/5/6/8/10 visually read. Certificate dated 22 June 1960 states that in excess of 600 cars matching the application of 12 May were completed on 11 May, at least 33% with optional wire wheels. Base 2548 cc controls over other retrospective rounding. Cast-iron block is explicit: heritage wording about all-aluminium engines is not imported. Selected original manual base, not prototype 100002, later reinforced B/C-spec, automatic, steering/engine swaps or competition equipment. No unprinted power rating is invented.
cars.summary: The SP250 marked a radical sporting departure for Daimler, combining Edward Turner’s compact V8 with a fibreglass roadster body and four-wheel disc brakes. Its engine design and unusual break from the marque’s formal saloons make it a distinctive British performance-car landmark.

cars.variant: P1800 — February 1961 USA brochure, four-speed manual

Selected original 1.78-litre, 100 SAE bhp at 5500 rpm, 108 lb-ft at 4000 rpm and four-speed without optional OD. No invented SAE-net/kW conversion or substitution of later 108/115/120-hp, 2.0-litre, injected E, automatic or ES-estate data. Contemporary American import/distributor footer defines market. cars.summary: The P1800 gave Volvo a distinctive international sports-car identity through Pelle Petterson’s Italian-influenced coupe design and its association with Simon Templar in The Saint. The original Jensen-assembled, B18-powered car established a durable grand-touring icon that developed through the later 1800S and 1800E.

cars.variant: Giulietta Sprint Speciale — FIA 122 base 1290-cc road reference
cars.specification_market: Original Alfa Romeo/Automobile Club d’Italia base application CSAI AR 13, FIA 122 GT; 14-page file. Cover and base engine/cam/gearbox/performance PDF1/3/4/6/7 individually read after full contact sheet. Declared 1290 cc, 100 DIN CV at 6500 rpm, twin cams and five speeds are retained. No claimed 200 km/h figure is used because factory retrospective gives a different road-speed narrative. Later valve/ratio extensions, Zagato SVZ/SZ and 1600-cc Giulia Sprint Speciale data are excluded. Body/photo illustrates the original Giulietta road family, not an additional first-series/body revision count.
cars.summary: The Giulietta Sprint Speciale translated Franco Scaglione’s aerodynamic design work for Bertone into an exceptional road coupe. A streamlined body, alloy twin-cam four and five-speed gearbox made it a distinctive small-capacity high-performance GT, positioned for long-distance road driving rather than the lighter Zagato competition role.
